key_insight: An agentic quality-control workflow reduces entity-grounding errors in LLM-generated biomedical ontology definitions, while logical inconsistencies remain harder to repair.
clinical_relevance: More reliable ontology definitions could support biomedical knowledge systems used in clinical NLP, but this study does not establish benefits for patient care.
method: Generate definitions and extract their implied axioms.
Measure entity grounding with Entity Error Rate and logical consistency with Logical Inconsistency Rate.
Use ontology-checking diagnostics to iteratively repair definitions.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on Disease Ontology, Uberon Ontology, and Uberon-ConstraintStress showed reduced entity errors while maintaining strong conventional text-generation performance.
watch_item: Logical checks revealed sparse failures missed by text-similarity metrics, but the workflow's ability to repair them remained limited.
paper_title: From Fluent Text to Ontology-Compatible Definitions: A Quality-Control Agentic Workflow
